notes: Modified cash basis village (basis cash). Governmental = Total Governmental Funds column p4; beginning/ending cash = beginning/ending fund balance (cash basis; includes certificates of deposit, restricted cash, county treasurer cash, so investments not shown separately). The Taxes line 667,830 (p4) is split using the general receipts on p2 (property 466,496, sales and use 146,048, motor vehicle 46,980, occupation 1,000, special assessment 7,306; sum 667,830). Intergovernmental 137,751 has no printed breakdown anywhere in the trimmed PDF, so it stays one state aid line. Governmental roll-forward: 1,480,516 + 1,152,122 - 1,195,001 + 196,556 - 244,272 = 1,389,921. Business-type = Water and Sewer, Total column p6, measure cash (modified cash net position); operating transfer in 47,716; roll-forward 442,445 + 237,003 - 438,146 + 47,716 = 289,018. Business-type receipts/disbursements have no single printed total, so computed. Balance sheet (re-check attempt 2, user rule 2026-10-27): the governmental funds Balance Sheet - Modified Cash Basis (p3) Total Governmental Funds column equals the government-wide governmental activities figures (total assets and fund balances 1,389,921 = p1 governmental net position), so governmental lines now come from p3 with fund balance by classification (Restricted 876,719, Assigned 488,197, Unassigned 25,005) instead of the government-wide Restricted/Unrestricted 876,719/513,202; business-type lines stay from the p1 Business-type Activities column (cash 128,137, CDs 160,881, unrestricted 289,018). Totals 1,678,939 are the p1 Total column; no liabilities. Detail: the p7 budgetary comparison schedule gives only fund-level actual totals (no lines; budget only as grand total 1,464,188 receipts / 2,633,450 disbursements) so it is not itemized into detail; Library 7,138 and Park 9,240 receipts there are inside Other Governmental on p4. Because no line-level budget schedule exists, per-fund Water and Sewer operating lines come from the p6 business-type statement and cover operating receipts and operating disbursements; the p6 nonoperating lines (interest income, loan payments, capital projects) are recorded per fund under a separate 'nonoperating' schedule name with no detail_totals, since the statement prints only a net nonoperating total (Water -282,775, Sewer -28,138; the lines tie to it). Transfer cross-check: interfund in 196,556 (General 25,000 from Keno; Street 44,935; Cemetery 13,116; Fire 2,509; Other Governmental 110,996) vs out 244,272 (General 161,479; Debt Service 57,793; Keno 25,000); net 47,716 equals the Water fund operating transfer in on p6 and the internal transfers on p2. All matched; no hidden transfers in spending lines. Statement p4 total column is as printed. Detail (user 2026-10-27): per-fund lines from the fund statements' columns (p4, p6) replace the combined schedule (the p6 per-fund business-type lines were already in; the Water operating transfer in 47,716 is added). Verifier fix (attempt 3, 2026-10-28): business-type 'User fees' 224,203 (p6) is category Utility Charges, matching its per-fund lines; the per-fund 'Taxes' lines on p4 (General 247,193, Street 1,239, Debt Service 419,398) are category/detail_category taxes (unlabeled), since the p2 tax-type breakdown is not by fund (property 466,496 less Debt Service 419,398 leaves at most 47,098 for the other funds, so the General line cannot be mostly property tax); the Cemetery Fund charges 3,950 are Cemetery Fees; the Keno Fund 'Charges for services' 15,387 (p2 groups it under Miscellaneous) is keno/lottery, marked review. The statement-level receipts keep the p2 split. Read pages 1-7 of 7
